name: Diotrephes
charge: Loving the preeminence; prating against the apostle with malicious words; casting the brethren out of the church
summary: John wrote to the congregation, but Diotrephes, who loved to have the preeminence among them, received them not (3 John 1:9). John said that if he came he would remember the deeds: prating against them with malicious words, refusing to receive the brethren, forbidding those who would, and casting them out of the congregation (3 John 1:10). No sentence is pronounced; John gives the rule instead, to follow not that which is evil but that which is good (3 John 1:11).
offenseFull: The teaching will not let the verse pass lightly. This was a man the apostles themselves had set up, an overseer over a congregation, and the men he would not receive had walked with Christ, eaten with him, and been taught by him. The sin is named as covetousness, and not of money or a garment: he coveted power. He wanted to be the top teacher in Israel and to be known as number one, and he could not work with anybody who might be greater or know more than he did. Zimri had the same spirit and killed a drunken king to sit on the throne, and then destroyed the whole house of Baasha (1 Kings 16:8-12). Diotrephes did not receive the apostles because he thought he was over them.

John lists the deeds. Prating against the apostles with malicious words is verbal abuse and name calling, the same evil that fills the internet now, men who learned a few scriptures running their mouths at the men who taught them. Refusing the brethren, forbidding them that would, and casting people out of the congregation is what it looks like on the ground (3 John 1:10). A man like this builds a clique out of the brothers who will not question him, raises them up, and pushes away the ones who come asking from the scriptures; the clique keeps evil quiet in the midst and the whole thing turns into partiality. Then, when brothers are sent to check on a school, he tells them today is not a good day, come back another time, and any member who goes over his head is put out. Paul warned the overseers of it at Miletus: after his departing grievous wolves would enter in, not sparing the flock, and of their own selves men would arise speaking perverse things to draw away disciples after them (Acts 20:28-30).
judgmentFull: John pronounces no sentence on him. He gives the congregation the rule instead: follow not that which is evil, but that which is good; he that does good is of God, but he that does evil has not seen God (3 John 1:11). The standard for a leader is the one Christ set. The princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion and the great ones authority, but it shall not be so among us; whoever will be great shall be the minister, and whoever will be chief shall be the servant (Matthew 20:25-27). He that is greatest among you shall be your servant, and the man who exalts himself shall be abased while the man who humbles himself shall be exalted (Matthew 23:11-12). Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall (Proverbs 16:18).

The answer the teaching keeps returning to is that there is only one preeminent. Christ is the head of the body, the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he might have the preeminence (Colossians 1:18). Not the bishop, not the captain, not Diotrephes. Gamaliel’s test applies to every man who rises up boasting himself to be somebody: Theudas drew four hundred after him and was slain, Judas of Galilee drew much people and perished, and all that obeyed them were scattered and brought to nothing, because if the work is of men it comes to nothing, and if it is of God it cannot be overthrown (Acts 5:34-39). Cursed is the man that trusts in man and makes flesh his arm (Jeremiah 17:5), so the men who followed such a leader away from the scriptures carry their own judgment. And the class sets him among the hirelings: the hireling is not the shepherd, the sheep are not his own, so he sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, because he cares not for the sheep (John 10:12-13). The brethren he shut out were the very strangers the body is commanded to entertain (Hebrews 13:2).

lawsResolved.text: Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
You are to speak evil of no man.
We are to be hospitable towards one another without grudging.
A minister must be blameless, vigilant, sober, just, holy, self-control led, of good behavior, given to hospitality, and able to teach and exhort.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.

text.text: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.
Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.
But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:
But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.
Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.
Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the apostles forth a little space;
And said unto them, Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.

For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.
After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.
And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:
But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.
Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord.
But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep.
The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
